subject.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle

question: Should OpenClaw adopt resetSessionEntryLifecycle as a permanent Plugin SDK/runtime contract with the proposed active-work fence, rollback, and locked-harness owner handoff semantics?
rationale: The Teams behavior is well supported, but the implementation deliberately exposes a reusable external API and defines cross-plugin session ownership semantics that automated review cannot make permanent without owner intent.

options.title: Approve the shared contract
options.body: Accept the owner-aware lifecycle-reset API, then refresh the branch and require exact-head session, Plugin SDK, Teams, and boundary validation before merge.

options.title: Narrow the exposed surface
options.body: Keep the Teams fix but replace the public subpath export with the narrowest owner-scoped runtime seam that does not create an unnecessary external plugin contract.

options.title: Pause the reset model
options.body: Keep the PR open until maintainers define a different canonical lifecycle-reset and locked-harness ownership model.

recommendation.title: Approve the shared contract
recommendation.body: Accept the owner-aware lifecycle-reset API, then refresh the branch and require exact-head session, Plugin SDK, Teams, and boundary validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They contributed the key personal-chat scope correction and are the clearest available owner candidate for the cross-cutting session/runtime contract.
